title: Johann Gerlach, Occulta scripta chymica, Wellcome MS.309 (catalogue 1252): alchemical recipes in a 52-label homophonic sign cipher, pp.7-10, 13-19 and parts of pp.40, 107, 112, 115, 156, 177 read with Kohn's key of 1889 (read in part)

steps.what: Catalogue entry 1252 (UK libraries sweep, 28-29 Oct 2026): Wellcome MS.309, 178 pages in a cipher, Kohn's key inserted at pp.260-261; not viewed then.

Kohn's key (1889, pp.260-261, scans 0265-0266) set up as a table of 52 sign labels with a letter each (key_v3): signs only on the sheet, so values by the order of the groups; the u, t, s groups moved one step against Kohn's order to fit the text; three figure-4 shapes told apart by context.
Sign-by-sign transcription of pp.7-10, 13-19 and parts of six later pages from the Wellcome IIIF scans: 348 lines, 6,479 lettered signs, 143 doubtful.

Real-word test: decoded words (2+ letters, no unknown sign) looked up in 64,029 sixteenth-century spellings: 77% (p.40) to 96% (p.112) per page; 1,000 shuffled keys per page reach at most 30% (p.112) and 26% (p.40). Contributor's figures; the word list and scorer were not sent.

Blind control on p.8: transcribed and decoded once with the key frozen, by the contributor's record: 529 signs, signs in words giving sense 489 firm (92.4%), 522 with probable readings (98.7%). Independent transcribers agree on 91.6% to 99.6% of signs.

The decode built into Early New High German sentences and translated for each page: recipes for flowers of sulphur (pp.7-10), flowers of antimony (pp.13-15), the 'corruption of Sol' with sal ammoniac, spiritus vini and aqua regis (pp.16-19), and the openings of later sections. Contributor's counts per page: firm 80.5% to 96.1% of signs on the five rated pages; pp.14-18 and the partial pages not rated.

Integration after an independent check from the issue text: own decoder written from the key table reproduces all 348 decoded lines from the sign transcription (0 differences, 6,479 signs); Kohn's two key leaves and the first six lines of p.8 compared with the Wellcome IIIF images; word-level count by the README rule from reading.md: 1,259 of 1,395 words read without a doubt mark or bracket = 90.3%. Not re-run: the word-list test and shuffles (list not sent).

outcome.method_basis: Kohn's key of 1889, filed in the volume itself (pp.260-261), applied to the sign transcription by the contributor: the key is not recovered here. The sheet carries signs in groups without letters, so the table is the contributor's alignment of its order to the alphabet, with three groups re-aligned and three figure-4 shapes assigned by context.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md, words of the 17 pages and parts: 1,259 of 1,395 read with no '?' and no bracketed supply or hole = 90.3% (holes: words with a doubtful letter, supplied or restored words, gaps; recounted at integration, 12 Nov 2026). The contributor's sign-level figures are firm 92.4% (p.8), 80.5% (p.9), 86.2% (p.10), 96.1% (p.13), 95.7% (p.19), 'probable' 97% to 99%; those are his rule, not the README's.

credits.note: his key of 1889 on pp.260-261 of Wellcome MS.309, applied here as a table of sign labels (key_v3)

gaps.detail: these signs do not occur in the pages read; the values are as the sheet gives them by order, untested.

texts.label: Gerlach, Occulta scripta chymica, pp.7-10, 13-19 and parts of pp.40, 107, 112, 115, 156, 177
texts.summary: Alchemical and medical recipes of a 1570s German notebook: how to make flowers of sulphur and to prepare sublimed sulphur three times with colcothar and salt as a medicine for the lungs and chest (pp.7-10), flowers of antimony red and white, with a fever remedy (pp.13-15), how to make quicksilver out of gold, and the numbered preparations 'belonging to the corruption of Sol': sal ammoniac sublimed through rock salt, spiritus vini from burnt wine and tartar, and aqua regis (pp.16-19); the openings of later sections on the philosopher's stone, putrefaction, the mercury of Sol and Luna and the arcanum of tartar are read in part.

reading_review.by: integration reader for the project (a model session, not a person), 12 Nov 2026
reading_review.note: Read as Early New High German sentences against decryption.txt and translation.md on pp.7, 8, 13 and 19: coherent recipe prose with the technical vocabulary of the time (schwewel, colcothar, uitriol, sublimir, helm, viola, weinstein). p.9 and p.10 hold stained or damaged lines with real holes. The pages are the contributor's reading of a 52-label table he aligned himself to Kohn's sheet; the decode is reproduced from his own transcription, which was compared with the image on six lines of p.8 only.

prior.where: A key by Julius Kohn (1889) is written into the volume (pp.260-261), so the cipher was known to be solvable and its key was recorded; the Wellcome catalogue says 'Kohn's key inserted'. No published reading found by the contributor (10-11 Nov 2026); German specialist literature, Kohn's papers and the Wellcome files not checked.

human: Malcolm McBratney directed the work and sent the result as GitHub issue #439; Claude and, for three pages, other model sessions transcribed from the images, applied the key, decoded and read. No reading by a person without AI.
